items.title: Smooth covariant 2-tensor fields on a smooth manifold
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]), with smooth atlas
$\mathcal A$ and maximal smooth atlas $[\mathcal A]$
([[def-smooth-atlas]], [[def-smoothly-compatible-charts]]). For $p\in M$ the
tangent space $T_pM$ is the real vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]), and the cotangent space is its
algebraic dual $T_p^*M:=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]).

A **covariant $2$-tensor at $p$** is a bilinear map
$A_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$. It is **symmetric** when
$A_p(v,w)=A_p(w,v)$ for all $v,w\in T_pM$, and **nondegenerate** when the only
$v\in T_pM$ with $A_p(v,w)=0$ for all $w\in T_pM$ is $v=0$.

A **smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$** is a family $A=(A_p)_{p\in M}$
assigning to each $p$ a covariant $2$-tensor $A_p$ at $p$, such that for every
chart $(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas $[\mathcal A]$ the **component
functions**

$$A_{ab}(q):=A_q\!\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^a}\Big|_q,\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x^b}\Big|_q\right),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$. Here $\partial/\partial x^a|_q$ is the coordinate
derivation at $q$ ([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]],
[[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the index
ranges over $a,b\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, and smoothness of the real-valued functions
$A_{ab}$ on the open set $U\subseteq M$ is the notion of
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] applied to $M$ and
$\mathbb R$.

Because the coordinate derivations at $q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), specifying
$A$ is the same as specifying the matrix of component functions in each chart;
[[lem-gr-covariant-two-tensor-transformation-law]] proves that the smoothness
requirement is independent of the chart used, so that the condition may be
checked on any smooth atlas of $M$, and derives the transformation law relating
components in two overlapping charts.

The field is **symmetric** when $A_p$ is symmetric for every $p\in M$, which in
a chart is the identity $A_{ab}=A_{ba}$ of component functions; it is
**nondegenerate** when $A_p$ is nondegenerate for every $p$, which in a chart is
the nonvanishing at every point of the polynomial function
$\det(A_{ab})$ of the components. The **matrix** of $A$ in a chart means the
matrix $\bigl(A_{ab}(q)\bigr)$ of its component functions at $q$.

**Convention.** In the four-dimensional case $n=4$ used in this library, indices
are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ with $0$ the distinguished time index, and we write
$A_{ab}$ for the components. A covariant $2$-tensor field is also called a
**$(0,2)$ tensor field**.
items.strategy: Define smooth (0,2) tensor fields by chart components over the maximal atlas, after fixing tangent spaces as derivations and declaring the symmetry and nondegeneracy reading; the chart-independence of the definition and the transformation law are proved in the companion lemma, so the definition is chart-independent rather than merely chart-wise.

items.title: Chart independence and the transformation law of a smooth covariant 2-tensor field
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold and let $A=(A_p)_{p\in M}$ be a family
assigning to each $p$ a covariant $2$-tensor at $p$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Suppose that the component
functions of $A$ are $C^\infty$ in the charts of one smooth atlas of $M$. Let
$(U,x)$ and $(V,y)$ be overlapping smooth charts of the maximal smooth atlas and
let $A_{cd}$ and $A'_{ab}$ denote the components of $A$ in the charts $x$ and
$y$. Then for every $q\in U\cap V$, writing $y=q$ in the second chart,

$$A'_{ab}(y) = \sum_{c,d=1}^{n}\frac{\partial x^c}{\partial y^a}(y)\,\frac{\partial x^d}{\partial y^b}(y)\,A_{cd}\bigl(x(y)\bigr),$$

where $\partial x^c/\partial y^a$ are the entries of the total derivative
$D(x\circ y^{-1})(y)$. In particular $A$ is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field
on $M$: its components are $C^\infty$ in every chart of the maximal smooth
atlas.
items.strategy: Direct computation: the chain rule expresses the coordinate derivations of one chart in the other, bilinearity of each A_p converts the change of frame into the displayed double-sum law, and smoothness of the transition and its Jacobian plus closure of C^∞ maps under products give chart-independence of smoothness.

items.title: Smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifolds: the geometric objects of the model
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future closed null cone is
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.
items.strategy: Fix the model data (M,g,N): a smooth boundaryless four-manifold, a smooth symmetric nondegenerate (0,2) field of inertia (3,1,0) at every point, and a smooth timelike field as time orientation; record the pointwise causal vocabulary, the two-component timelike cone, and define future/past by the sign of the pairing with N, deferring the exhaustiveness proof to the companion lemma.

items.title: The inverse metric, musical isomorphisms and index raising
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b=\delta^c{}_bg^{ab}(q),$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.
items.strategy: Pointwise linear algebra of a nondegenerate form: the flat map is an isomorphism by trivial kernel and equal dimensions, the inverse metric is its transport to the dual space, and components, index positions and the metric trace are fixed by the matrix identity g^{ac}g_{cb}=delta^a_b; smoothness of the components is deferred to the companion lemma.

items.title: Smoothness and transformation of the inverse-metric components
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$g_p^{-1}$ and $g^{ab}$ be the inverse metric and its chart components as in
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]. Then:

1. For every smooth chart $(U,x)$ the component functions $g^{ab}:U\to\mathbb R$
   are $C^\infty$ on $U$.
2. For overlapping smooth charts $(U,x)$, $(V,y)$ the components satisfy the
   contravariant transformation law

$$g'^{ab}(y)=\sum_{c,d=1}^{4}\frac{\partial y^a}{\partial x^c}\bigl(x(y)\bigr)\, \frac{\partial y^b}{\partial x^d}\bigl(x(y)\bigr)\,g^{cd}\bigl(x(y)\bigr),\qquad y\in y(U\cap V),$$

where $\partial y^a/\partial x^c$ are the entries of $D(y\circ x^{-1})$.

3. Consequently the pointwise bilinear forms $g_p^{-1}$ on $T_p^*M$ are
   presented by component functions that are smooth in every chart and glue by
   the contravariant law; the inverse metric is a well-defined smooth component
   family determined by $g$ alone.
items.strategy: Direct: the component matrix is smooth with nowhere-zero determinant, so its inverse is smooth by the adjugate formula for matrix inversion; the transformation law is obtained by inverting the covariant law G' = J^T G J and identifying J^{-1} with the Jacobian of the reverse transition by the chain rule.

items.title: SI unit and coordinate conventions of the classical gravitational framework
items.statement:
This item fixes the unit and coordinate conventions used when the geometric
objects of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and the tensor fields of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] are read as a classical
gravitational model. It is a statement of conventions, not a physical law and
not a measurement.

**(a) Constants.** The framework uses the conversion constant $c>0$ with SI
dimension $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, the Newton constant $G_N>0$ with
dimension $\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$, and a signed
cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ with dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$. Neither the
numerical value of $c$ nor that of $G_N$ is asserted by this item; the signs
and dimensions are part of the conventions. The coupling constant that appears
in the field law adopted later in the framework is

$$\kappa:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4},$$

with dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^{2}$; consequently
$\kappa T$ has dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$ when the components $T_{ab}$ of a
stress-energy tensor in a $g$-orthonormal frame are measured in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$.

**(b) Coordinates.** A smooth chart $(U,x)$ may be chosen in either of two
standard ways. In **length coordinates** one sets $x^0=ct$ with $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$
all measured in metres; then the metric components $g_{ab}$ are dimensionless,
$ds^2:=g_{ab}dx^adx^b$ has dimension $\mathrm m^2$, the Christoffel symbols
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and curvature components and
the scalar curvature have dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$. In **time coordinates**
one sets $x^0=t$ in seconds; then $g_{00}$ carries dimension
$\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$ and the remaining components need not share a
dimension. Angular coordinates or mixed coordinates change individual
component dimensions by the Jacobians of the coordinate change; there is no
universal dimension attached to a single component of a tensor in a general
chart. The $g$-orthonormal frames of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]
are the frames in which components have the invariant dimensional readings
below.

**(c) Invariant quantities.** The following readings are part of the
conventions: $ds^2$ in $\mathrm m^2$; proper time $\tau$ in seconds;
four-velocity components $U^a=dx^a/d\tau$ in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$;
$g$-orthonormal components $T_{ab}$ of a stress-energy tensor in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; energy densities $T_{ab}n^an^b$ for unit timelike
$n$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; the cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ in
$\mathrm m^{-2}$; and the curvature components $R^a{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$
and $R$ in $\mathrm m^{-2}$.

**(d) Natural units.** The cited treatments frequently set $c=1$ and
sometimes $G_N=1$, equating units of length and time and, in the second case,
of mass and length. Such a choice is a shorthand for the conventions of
parts (a)-(c): a dimensionful result obtained in natural units must have the
factors of $c$ (and of $G_N$) restored before it is compared with an SI
quantity, and statements in this framework are stated with those factors
present. Natural-unit forms of equations are read as the corresponding SI forms
with the constants restored; the numerical value $c=1$ in one coordinate is
the coordinate statement $x^0=x^1$ in length coordinates for a null ray, not a
change of the physical constant.
items.strategy: A conventions item: fix the dimensions of c, G_N, Lambda and kappa, the two standard coordinate readings (x^0 = ct metres versus x^0 = t seconds), the invariant dimensional readings, and the rule that natural-unit expressions must have the constants restored; it asserts no measured value and adopts no law.
items.physical_scope: Conventions for writing the smooth Lorentzian geometry of this framework with SI dimensions: conversion constant c, Newton constant G_N, cosmological parameter Lambda, coordinates, components and invariants. The conventions fix dimensions and unit restoration only; they assert no measured value, adopt no field law, and make no claim about nature.

items.title: Metric compatibility, torsion freedom and the metric-selected connection class
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.
items.strategy: Define g-compatibility by the Leibniz identity for smooth vector fields, torsion freedom by vanishing of the torsion tensor, and the metric-selected class as the intersection; no existence or uniqueness claim is made, and the equivalent chart forms are proved in the companion lemma.

items.title: Classification of future and past causal vectors by a timelike field
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Write
$N_p^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,N_p)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and let $T_p$ be the
timelike set, with components $C_p^+$ (the one containing $N_p$) and $C_p^-$,
and with future and past causality as fixed in
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]] and
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Then:

1. $N_p^{\perp}$ is a $3$-dimensional linear subspace of $T_pM$, and $g_p$ is
   positive definite on it; equivalently, every nonzero $v\in T_pM$ with
   $g_p(v,N_p)=0$ is spacelike.
2. $g_p(v,N_p)\neq0$ for every nonzero causal $v\in T_pM$.
3. $C_p^+=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\text{ and }g_p(v,N_p)<0\}$, and
   $C_p^-=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\text{ and }g_p(v,N_p)>0\}$.
4. A nonzero $v\in T_pM$ is causal and future-directed if and only if
   $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)$, and causal and past-directed if and only if
   $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)$. Consequently
   $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$ is exactly the set of
   future-directed causal vectors and $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)\setminus\{0\}$
   exactly the set of past-directed causal vectors,
   $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\cap\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)=\{0\}$, and every
   nonzero causal vector is exactly one of future-directed and past-directed.
items.strategy: Direct computation in an orthonormal basis chosen with positive time component for N: Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the spatial pairing, so no nonzero causal vector is orthogonal to N; the component descriptions of the timelike cone then identify the future component with the sign condition g(v,N)<0, and an explicit perturbation exhibits null boundary vectors in the closure; the past side is the mirror computation.

items.title: Torsion freedom and metric compatibility in chart components
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $\nabla$ be an affine connection on
$M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) and let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, with Christoffel symbols $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a
\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$ ([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]])
and metric components $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$. Then:

1. $\nabla$ is torsion-free ([[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]])
   if and only if $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\Gamma^a{}_{cb}$ for all $a,b,c$ in every
   smooth chart.
2. $\nabla$ is $g$-compatible ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) if and
   only if, in every smooth chart,

$$\partial_ag_{bc}=\sum_{d=1}^{4}\bigl(\Gamma^d{}_{ab}g_{dc}+\Gamma^d{}_{ac}g_{bd}\bigr) \qquad(a,b,c=1,\dots,4).$$

Thus $\nabla$ is metric-selected for $(M,g)$ if and only if both displayed
conditions hold in every smooth chart.
items.strategy: Two local computations: torsion on coordinate pairs is the antisymmetric part of the Christoffel symbols by vanishing of coordinate brackets, and C^∞-bilinearity reduces the general torsion to coordinate pairs; metric compatibility evaluated on coordinate fields gives the displayed identity in one direction, and expanding arbitrary smooth fields in the coordinate frame in the other direction reduces the Leibniz identity to the same component equation.

items.title: Stress-energy tensor field of a model
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset, the **matter domain** of the model,
carrying the restricted smooth structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]].

A **stress-energy tensor field** on $U$ for the model is a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on $U$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]: at every $p\in U$, $T_p$ is a
symmetric bilinear form $T_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$ varying smoothly with
$p$, with component functions $T_{ab}=T(\partial_a,\partial_b)$ in every smooth
chart of $U$. No nondegeneracy of $T_p$ is required or implied; in particular
$T_p$ may have radical, as it does for a dust model whose stress-energy form
vanishes on a hyperplane.

**Unit reading.** In any $g_p$-orthonormal ordered basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ with $e_0$ timelike — such bases exist by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] — the numbers $T(e_a,e_b)$ are
the components of $T$ in that frame, and by the conventions of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]] they are measured in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. The framework reads these components as energy
density ($T(e_0,e_0)$), energy flux and momentum density ($T(e_0,e_i)$ and
$T(e_i,e_0)$, equal by symmetry) and stress ($T(e_i,e_j)$). This reading is
part of the physical interpretation of the model, not a mathematical
consequence: components in a different orthonormal frame are related by the
corresponding Lorentz transformation of the frame and generally differ.

**Relation to the matter model.** This item defines the slot that a matter
model fills. The identity of $T$ for a given model — its expression in terms of
the model's fields and its equation of motion — comes from that model and is
not part of this definition; for a model derived from an action, $T$ is the
Hilbert stress-energy tensor of that action, while a model that prescribes $T$
by hand is a separate source model subject to the consistency conditions of the
adopted gravitational field law. Nothing here asserts that a prescribed smooth
symmetric $T$ is realized by any matter model, that $T$ is conserved, or that
$T$ satisfies any positivity condition; conservation and the energy conditions
are separate statements, the latter defined separately in this framework.

**Scope limitations.** The definition is confined to the smooth branch: a
matter distribution whose density fails to be smooth across a surface, a
distributional point source, or a source supported on a hypersurface is not a
stress-energy tensor field of this definition, and such configurations require
additional distributional or junction mathematics not supplied here. The
matter domain $U$ is an idealization of the region occupied by matter; the
model may also include matter sources described on all of $M$ or on a union of
several such domains.
items.strategy: Define the stress-energy slot of a model: a smooth symmetric covariant 2-tensor field on an open matter domain with the orthonormal-frame unit reading in J m^-3; explicitly permit degeneracy, place the identification of T for any matter branch outside the definition, and exclude distributional and lower-dimensional sources from the smooth branch.
items.physical_scope: The tensor slot for the matter content of a classical smooth gravitational model: a smooth symmetric covariant 2-tensor field on the model's matter domain, with the framework's unit reading. The item defines the object and its units only; which field configuration realizes it, and whether it satisfies any positivity or conservation identity, is a separate matter assumption.

items.title: The pointwise energy conditions WEC, NEC, DEC and SEC
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$T$ be a stress-energy tensor field on its matter domain
$U\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]), and let $\sharp_p$ and
$\operatorname{tr}_g$ be the musical isomorphism and the metric trace of
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]. For $p\in U$ and
$v\in T_pM$ write $T_p(v,\cdot)\in T_p^*M$ for the covector
$w\mapsto T_p(v,w)$, and recall that, by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]], a vector
$w\in T_pM$ lies in $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)$ exactly when $w=0$ or $w$ is
future-directed and causal, where $C_p^+$ is the component of the timelike set
containing $N_p$.

The model **satisfies at $p$**:

- the **weak energy condition (WEC)** when $T_p(v,v)\ge0$ for every timelike
  $v\in T_pM$;
- the **null energy condition (NEC)** when $T_p(v,v)\ge0$ for every null
  $v\in T_pM$;
- the **dominant energy condition (DEC)** when
  $-\sharp_p\bigl(T_p(v,\cdot)\bigr)\in\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)$ for every
  future-directed timelike $v\in T_pM$;
- the **strong energy condition (SEC)** when
  $\bigl(T_p-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_g(T)(p)\,g_p\bigr)(v,v)\ge0$ for every
  timelike $v\in T_pM$, that is, when
  $T_p(v,v)-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_g(T)(p)\,g_p(v,v)\ge0$.

The model **satisfies the condition** (on $U$) when the corresponding
inequality holds at every $p\in U$.

Each is a pointwise condition on the pair $(g_p,T_p)$ alone, evaluated on
timelike or null vectors as displayed; the expressions use only the metric
pairing $g_p$, its inverse pairing on covectors, and the endomorphism
$A^\sharp_p$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]. The
timelike and null vector sets are those of the Lorentz vector space
$(T_pM,g_p)$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).
items.strategy: Define the four pointwise conditions on (g_p,T_p) for the displayed vector classes, using the musical isomorphism and the metric trace; add that they are optional assumptions, not automatic, and that no implication among them is asserted.
items.physical_scope: Pointwise inequalities that a model may adopt for its stress-energy tensor: weak, null, dominant and strong energy conditions, stated for the smooth tensor fields of this framework. They are additional assumptions available to a model; no condition is automatic, no implication between them is asserted here, and their measured relevance is a separate empirical question.

items.title: Two time orientations agree or are opposite on each connected set
items.statement:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $N,N'$ be two smooth
timelike vector fields on $M$, so that both $(M,g,N)$ and $(M,g,N')$ are
time-oriented ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Put
$f(p):=g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ for $p\in M$, and for each $p$ let $C_p^+(N)$ and
$C_p^+(N')$ be the components of the timelike set of $T_pM$ containing $N_p$
and $N'_p$. Then:

1. $f:M\to\mathbb R$ is $C^\infty$ and $f(p)\neq0$ for every $p\in M$.
2. On every nonempty connected subset $C\subseteq M$ the function $f$ has
   constant sign: either $f<0$ throughout $C$ or $f>0$ throughout $C$.
3. If $f<0$ on a nonempty connected subset $C$, then
   $C_p^+(N')=C_p^+(N)$ and the future-directed causal vectors of $N'$ agree
   with those of $N$ at every $p\in C$; if $f>0$ on $C$, then
   $C_p^+(N')=C_p^-(N)$ and the future-directed causal vectors of $N'$ are
   exactly the past-directed causal vectors of $N$ at every $p\in C$.
4. In particular $N$ and $-N$ define opposite future cones at every point.
items.strategy: Direct: the pairing f = g(N,N') is smooth with nowhere-zero values, hence of constant sign on connected sets by the separation characterisation of connectedness; the sign decides whether N' lies in the future or the past cone of N, and the two-component structure converts that into equality or opposition of the future cones.

items.title: Adopted spacetime model and classical domain of the gravitational framework
items.statement:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework the
following statements.

**(i) Spacetime model.** The spacetime of a model of the framework is a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ as in
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: a smooth four-manifold $M$ without
boundary, a Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and a time orientation $N$. Its points represent
idealized physical events; the vector $N$ fixes which causal directions are
future-directed; and the causal classification of tangent vectors along any
worldline is the classification of the Lorentz vector spaces $(T_pM,g_p)$
together with the future/past convention of the time orientation. The metric
$g$ is the gravitational field of the model: it is the object that the field
law of the framework constrains, and its curvature is the model's
representation of gravity. The rules by which ideal clocks, test bodies and
light rays couple to $g$ are adopted separately as physical assumptions of the
framework.

**(ii) Classical domain.** Geometry and matter are treated as classical
continuum fields: the model describes macroscopic configurations of matter and
a classical metric, with no quantum description of either. The framework makes
no claim that a real spacetime is exactly such a manifold, that matter is
exactly a classical continuum, or that the smooth description applies to
arbitrarily small scales or arbitrarily strong fields; those are domain
limitations of the model family, not consequences of it.

**(iii) Unity of the model.** A model of the framework is specified by its
geometry $(M,g,N)$ together with its matter content and the field law adopted
for it; the geometry alone selects no matter configuration and no dynamics
(the matter assumptions are
adopted separately, in the companion postulate on matter content). Physical
parameters enter through
the unit conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]; no
numerical value of a constant is asserted here.

**(iv) Smooth-branch restriction.** The fields of a model are defined on an
open domain of $M$; the metric is $C^\infty$ on all of $M$ and $M$ has no
boundary. Configurations in which a field fails to be smooth on a nonempty open
set, in which matter is concentrated on a lower-dimensional set in a way that
produces a distributional stress-energy tensor, or in which $M$ carries a
boundary, are outside the stated smooth domain of the framework and require
mathematics not supplied by these postulates.

**(v) Status.** These are adopted assumptions. They are not derived from the
mathematics of manifolds, from any symmetry principle, or from experiment; the
equivalence principle and covariance arguments motivate but do not prove them.
Testing the framework means comparing predictions computed from a fully
specified model — geometry, matter content and field law — with observations,
and agreement is evidence about the model, not a proof of these postulates.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it adopts the smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold as the classical arena, with its continuum, smooth-branch, boundaryless and four-dimensional restrictions and its status as adopted rather than deduced; no dynamics, no parameter value and no empirical claim are asserted.
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of the framework as the spacetime of a classical model, with the framework's classical continuum domain and its smooth-branch and four-dimensional restrictions. Excludes quantum-gravity and quantum-field regimes, weak-regularity or singular regions, distributional sources, boundaries, and dimensions other than four. Adoption is a model assumption, not a derived or empirical result.

items.title: Adopted matter-content assumptions: fields, equations, stress-energy and energy conditions
items.statement:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, in
addition to [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]], the following statements
about the matter content of a model.

**(i) Matter content is model input.** A model of the framework specifies its
nongravitational fields or matter and their explicit equations of motion and
couplings. The geometric data $(M,g,N)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and covariance of the model's equations
under relabelling of events do not select those fields, equations or couplings:
different matter specifications over the same geometry are different models of
the framework, and no dynamical selection principle is asserted.

**(ii) Smooth matter and its stress-energy tensor.** The matter of a model on
its matter domain is represented by smooth fields on an open domain
$U\subseteq M$, and the model's stress-energy tensor is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on $U$ of
[[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]], with the unit reading recorded there.
The relation of $T$ to the matter fields is part of the model: a model derived
from an action defines $T$ as the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of that action,
while a model that prescribes $T$ directly is a separate source model.

**(iii) Consistency with the field law.** Where a model prescribes $T$
independently of matter fields, the prescription is admissible only if it meets
the consistency conditions imposed by the gravitational field law adopted for
the model, stated where that law is stated; in the action formulation the
matter equations, their coupling to the metric, and the on-shell conservation
of $T$ are derived within the model rather than assumed. Conservation is an
on-shell statement about a specified model and is not automatic for an
arbitrary smooth symmetric $T$.

**(iv) Energy conditions are optional additional assumptions.** A model may
adopt any of the pointwise inequalities of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]] as
further assumptions on its stress-energy tensor. None of them is a consequence
of the preceding clauses, of the field law, or of the symmetry of $T$; each
model records which conditions, if any, it adopts, and a model that adopts none
is not thereby excluded.

**(v) Scope and exclusions.** Idealizations such as unmodeled self-force,
finite-size and tidal corrections, dispersion, dissipation, and quantum effects
are outside the framework unless the model's explicit equations include them;
matter concentrated in a distributional or lower-dimensional source, and
matter configurations whose fields fail to be smooth on the model domain, are
outside the stated smooth branch and require additional mathematics. The
adoption of a matter model is not a claim that it describes nature.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it records that matter fields, their equations and couplings, and the stress-energy tensor are model input; that prescribed stress-energy is admissible only under the consistency conditions of the adopted field law; that energy conditions are optional; and that distributional sources and unmodelled corrections lie outside the smooth branch.
items.physical_scope: Matter-content assumptions of a classical smooth gravitational model: the nongravitational fields and their explicit equations and couplings are model input; matter is represented by smooth fields whose stress-energy tensor occupies the slot of the stress-energy definition; consistency with the adopted field law and optional energy conditions. Excludes quantum matter, distributional or lower-dimensional sources in the smooth branch, unmodeled self-force, finite-size and tidal corrections, dispersion and dissipation, and any claim that a particular matter model describes nature.

items.title: Primitive, adopted and derived status of the objects of the framework page
items.statement:
## Status audit

This remark records the status of the notions introduced on the
framework-and-geometry page. It is bookkeeping: it asserts no physical law and
no empirical claim, and every mathematical statement it repeats is proved in
the item cited.

**Primitive mathematical structure of a model.** The triple $(M,g,N)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: the smooth boundaryless four-manifold
$M$ with its smooth structure, the Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, and the time orientation $N$, a smooth nowhere-zero timelike
vector field. These are the primitive geometric data; the definition names no
equation that $g$ must satisfy.

**Adopted physical assumptions on this page.** The reading of $(M,g,N)$ as the
spacetime of a classical continuum model, with the stated smooth-branch and
four-dimensional restrictions, is the postulate
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]]; the statement that a model's
nongravitational matter content, its equations and its stress-energy tensor are
model input, together with the optional adoption of energy conditions, is the
postulate [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]. The unit and coordinate
conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]] are part of the
formulation; they fix dimensions and contain no measured value. The
stress-energy slot [[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]] and the energy-condition
inequalities [[def-gr-energy-conditions]] are formulation-level definitions
available to a model; a model that uses an energy condition adopts it as an
extra assumption.

**Derived (constructed, not adopted) on this page.** The inverse metric, the
musical isomorphisms $\flat_p,\sharp_p$, the raised and lowered component
conventions and the metric trace
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]), with the smoothness and
transformation law of the inverse-metric components
([[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]]); the pointwise causal classification of
tangent vectors; the future/past classification of nonzero causal vectors by
$N$, the identification of the future closed null cone with
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$, and the fact that a nonzero causal
vector has nonzero pairing with any timelike vector
([[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]); the agreement or
opposition of two time orientations on connected sets
([[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]); the
component form of torsion freedom and metric compatibility
([[lem-gr-connection-conditions-in-chart-components]]). These are mathematical
constructions and theorems from the primitive structure; they carry no
empirical content.

**Named but not constructed on this page.** The metric-selected connection
class of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] is defined by its two
conditions. This page neither asserts that a metric-selected connection exists
for a given $g$ nor that it is unique; the selection theorem is proved where
the connection of the model is constructed, and this page does not use that
conclusion. In particular no geodesic, proper-time or curvature construction
rests on the present page.

**Explicitly not claimed on this page.** No field law, no matter branch or
matter equation, no conservation identity for $T$, no field-equation
consistency condition, no clock, test-body or light-ray coupling, no
differentiable-structure result about worldlines, and no empirical statement.
Those are adopted or proved on later pages of the framework, each with its own
hypotheses.

**Time-orientation caveat.** Existence of the smooth timelike field $N$ is
adopted as part of the model data. It is an additional global condition: this
page does not prove that every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold carries a smooth
nowhere-zero timelike vector field, and the framework restricts to models for
which one is specified. Where a physical or mathematical development needs
time orientability, it states that hypothesis explicitly.
items.strategy: A status remark: it repeats, without proof obligations, the primitive, adopted, derived and not-claimed classification of the page's objects, and records the time-orientability caveat that existence of the smooth timelike field is adopted model data rather than a theorem of this page.
items.physical_scope: Status audit of the framework-and-geometry page: which objects are primitive model data, which statements are adopted postulates, which are constructed, and which are explicitly not claimed here. Bookkeeping only; it asserts no physical law, no empirical claim and no mathematical result beyond the items it cites.

items.title: The constant Minkowski metric as a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian manifold
items.statement:
Let $M:=\mathbb R^4$ with its standard smooth structure, for which the identity
map $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ is a global smooth chart
([[ex-euclidean-spaces-and-open-subsets-as-smooth-manifolds]]). Define the
family $A=(A_p)_{p\in M}$ by declaring its components in this chart to be the
constants

$$A_{ab}:=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab},\qquad\text{that is}\qquad A_p(v,w)=-v^0w^0+v^1w^1+v^2w^2+v^3w^3$$

for $v=\sum_av^a\partial_a|_p$, $w=\sum_aw^a\partial_a|_p$. Then $(M,A)$ is a
smooth Lorentzian four-manifold in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the field
$N:=\partial/\partial x^0$ is a time orientation, so $(M,A,N)$ is a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold; and at every $p$ the
future-directed causal vectors are exactly the nonzero $v$ with
$v^0\ge\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert=( (v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2 )^{1/2}$. In
particular $v_{(1)}:=(1,0,0,0)$ is future timelike, $v_{(2)}:=(1,1,0,0)$ is
future null and $v_{(3)}:=(0,1,0,0)$ is spacelike.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation: constant components give smoothness, symmetry, determinant -1 and inertia (3,1,0); the constant field partial_0 is timelike; the future cone follows from the sign of the pairing with partial_0; the sample vectors are classified by their values v^0 and |v_vec|.

items.title: Flat metric components in a spherical coordinate chart
items.statement:
Let $(M,A)$ be the flat Lorentzian four-manifold of
[[ex-gr-minkowski-chart-as-a-lorentzian-manifold]], with global identity chart
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$. Let

$$W:=\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\subseteq\mathbb R^4,\qquad \Phi(u)=\bigl(u^0,\ u^1\sin u^2\cos u^3,\ u^1\sin u^2\sin u^3,\ u^1\cos u^2\bigr),$$

written $u=(t,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$. Then $\Phi:W\to\mathbb R^4$ is a smooth
injection with $\det D\Phi(u)=-r^2\sin\vartheta\neq0$ on $W$; its image
$\Phi(W)$ is open, and $y:=\Phi^{-1}:\Phi(W)\to W$ is a smooth chart on $M$
whose transition with the identity chart is $\Phi$. In this chart the
components of $A$ are

$$A'_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(-1,\ 1,\ r^2,\ r^2\sin^2\vartheta\right)_{ab},$$

so $A'_{00}=-1$, $A'_{11}=1$, $A'_{22}=r^2$, $A'_{33}=r^2\sin^2\vartheta$ and the
off-diagonal components vanish. In particular the component functions are
smooth on $W$, $\det(A'_{ab})=-r^4\sin^2\vartheta<0$ on $W$, and the
diagonal signs exhibit inertia $(3,1,0)$; the metric is Lorentzian as read in
the spherical chart, and the components are non-constant although the same
metric has constant components in the identity chart.
items.strategy: Direct computation: the map Phi is shown injective with nonsingular differential, so it is a chart transition by the inverse function theorem; the transformation law evaluated on the Jacobian columns gives diag(-1,1,r^2,r^2 sin^2 theta), with off-diagonal terms vanishing by the pairwise orthogonality of the spherical coordinate derivatives.

items.title: The coordinate connection of the flat chart is metric-selected
items.statement:
Let $(M,A)$ be the flat Lorentzian four-manifold of
[[ex-gr-minkowski-chart-as-a-lorentzian-manifold]] with the global chart
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, and write $X=\sum_aX^a\partial_a$,
$Y=\sum_bY^b\partial_b$ for smooth vector fields. Define

$$\nabla_XY:=\sum_bX(Y^b)\,\partial_b .$$

Then $\nabla$ is an affine connection on $M$; its Christoffel symbols in the
global chart all vanish; and $\nabla$ is a metric-selected connection for
$(M,A)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]], that is, it is
torsion-free and $A$-compatible. This exhibits a nonempty
$\operatorname{LC}(M,A)$; the example claims no uniqueness of the element.
items.strategy: Direct computation: the operator nabla_X Y = sum_b X(Y^b) partial_b is verified to satisfy the connection axioms; its Christoffel symbols vanish; and the chart criteria for torsion freedom and metric compatibility are verified from the vanishing symbols and constant metric components.

items.title: A torsion-free connection that is not metric-compatible
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "every torsion-free affine connection on the flat
Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,A)$ of
[[ex-gr-minkowski-chart-as-a-lorentzian-manifold]] is compatible with the
metric $A$" ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

Counterexample: on the flat model, the affine connection with Gamma^0_{01} = Gamma^0_{10} = 1 and all other coefficients zero is torsion-free, but the compatibility identity fails at every point (0 on the left, -2 on the right).
items.strategy: Explicit witness: the connection with Gamma^0_{01} = Gamma^0_{10} = 1 and all other coefficients zero is verified to be an affine connection with symmetric coefficients, hence torsion-free, while the compatibility identity fails at every point because the left side is 0 and the right side is -2.

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.2, printed pp. 100-107 (PDF pp. 107-114)

items.title: Component units of the flat metric in length and time coordinates
items.statement:
Let $(M,A)$ be the flat Lorentzian four-manifold of
[[ex-gr-minkowski-chart-as-a-lorentzian-manifold]], whose global chart
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ is read as **length coordinates** $x^0=ct$,
$(x^1,x^2,x^3)=(x,y,z)$ in metres, with components
$A_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$, all dimensionless. Introduce the
**time coordinates** $u=(t,x,y,z)$, so that the coordinate change from $u$ to
$x$ is $x^0=cu^0$, $x^i=u^i$. Then in the chart $u$ the same field $A$ has
components

$$A'_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-c^2,1,1,1)_{ab},$$

the component $A'_{00}$ carries dimension $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$, the
components $A'_{ij}$ for $i,j\ge1$ are dimensionless, and the line element
$ds^2=A'_{ab}du^adu^b$ again has dimension $\mathrm m^2$. Thus the same metric
has components of different dimensions in the two charts, while its invariant
readings are unchanged; this verifies part (b) of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]].
items.strategy: Direct computation: the Jacobian of the change from x^0 = ct to x^0 = t is diagonal with entry c, so the time-time component changes to -c^2 with dimension m^2 s^-2 while ds^2 retains dimension m^2; the example asserts no numerical value of c.
items.physical_scope: Unit bookkeeping for the flat model metric under the change of time coordinate from x^0 = ct to x^0 = t: the metric components change from diag(-1,1,1,1) to diag(-c^2,1,1,1) and the component dimensions change accordingly, while the line element ds^2 retains dimension m^2. Illustrates the SI conventions; asserts no measured value of c and no dynamics.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), equations (1.5)-(1.6) with x^0 = ct and c = 1, and the remark that 1 second equals 3 x 10^8 metres in these units, printed pp. 4-5 (PDF pp. 11-12)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), Conventions: units with c = 1, PDF p. 1
D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), natural units and dimensions of constants, printed p. 144 (PDF p. 151)

items.title: A smooth symmetric nondegenerate 2-tensor field of inertia (2,2,0)
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "every smooth symmetric nondegenerate covariant $2$-tensor
field on a smooth four-manifold is a Lorentzian metric, so that
$g_p$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$ at every point"
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

Counterexample: the constant field diag(1,1,-1,-1) on R^4 is smooth, symmetric and nondegenerate with inertia (2,2,0), hence not Lorentzian.
items.strategy: Explicit witness: the constant field diag(1,1,-1,-1) on R^4 is smooth, symmetric and nondegenerate with determinant 1, but its inertia is (2,2,0) by inspection of the diagonal form, so it fails the Lorentzian signature condition; the Riemannian witness diag(1,1,1,1) is recorded alongside.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), the canonical form (2.34) and the distinction between Lorentzian and indefinite metrics, printed p. 49 (PDF p. 56)
K. Conrad, Bilinear Forms (orthogonality, radicals, inertia)

items.title: Reversing the time orientation reverses the future cone
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and put $N':=-N$. Then $(M,g,N')$ is
again a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and at every $p\in M$
the future-directed causal vectors of $N'$ are exactly the past-directed causal
vectors of $N$; equivalently $C_p^+(N')=C_p^-(N)$. In the flat model of
[[ex-gr-minkowski-chart-as-a-lorentzian-manifold]] with $N=\partial_0$, the
vector $\partial_0$ is future-directed for $N$ and past-directed for $-N$.
items.strategy: Direct: -N is smooth and timelike, so it is a time orientation; the pairing g(N,-N) = -g(N,N) is positive everywhere, which by the two-orientation lemma means the future cones are opposite; the flat-model evaluation on partial_0 exhibits a future vector of N that is past for -N.
